findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT- There were observed to be raw shell eggs on a bucket of pickles in the double-door cooler. CORRECTED- The eggs were moved to the bottom shelf of the cooler. Proper storage order was discussed. Ensure that food is protected from contamination during preparation, holding, storage, and display.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
FIRST REPEAT- The double door cooler in the facility is observed to have an ambient of 50F. The PIC stated that the temperature of the cooler was last checked at 9:15am and the temperature was approximately 40F. All TCS food items in the cooler were probed and the following items were discarded: 

1. A package of pepperoni at 51F. 
2. A container of ham at 52F. 
3. Three containers of turkey at 56F, 56F, and 52F. 
4. A container of cut tomatoes at 48F. 
5. Two packages of cheddar cheese at 52F and 53F. 
6. A package of meatballs at 51F. 
7. Five packages of provolone cheese at 50F, 52F, 51F, 53F, and 53F. 
8. A package of bacon at 50F.
9. Two containers of raw shelled eggs at 57F and 52F. 
10. Two containers of ranch that probed to be at 53F and 56F. 
11. Two containers of basil pesto at 55F and 56F. 
12. A package of potato soup at 50F. 
13. A bag of macaroni and cheese at 54F.
14. A container of hummus at 53F. 
15. A bag of chicken noodle soup at 52F. 
16. A container of veggie turkey at 55F. 
17. Two containers of roast beef at 51F. 
18. A container of Thousand Island Dressing at 49F. 
19. Two containers of meatballs and marinara at 53F. 
20. Three containers of marinara at 57F, 55F, and 53F. 

All TCS food items that were probed to be out of temperature were voluntarily discarded. Other TCS food items were prepared at around 11am and were placed under Time as Control. Discussed making sure to discard these items by 5pm. A follow up is scheduled regarding the double door cooler (see violation #33). Ensure that all TCS food items are held at 41F or under.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT- The double door cooler in the facility is observed to have an ambient temperature of 50F. The fan in the cooler is not spinning. The only cold holding units in the facility are this double door cooler, the preparation cooler, the lobby drink cooler, and the standing freezer. All TCS food items that were out of temperature were discarded or placed on time as control, while all other items were moved into the prep cooler (see violation #33). A follow up is scheduled for 6/17/2026 to ensure that the double door cooler has been repaired and is sufficiently holding all TCS food items at 41F and below. It is highly recommended to maintain a temperature log to routinely track the temperature of coolers to ensure that they are properly cold holding.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: During the calibration process (using the ice water method) of the facility’s only probe thermometer, the probe thermometer is observed to be approximately 10F out of calibration. While it should reach 32F during the ice bath, it was at approximately 22F. There was no tool that could twist the nut on the probe thermometer to calibrate it. A follow up is scheduled for 6/17/2026 to ensure that the probe thermometer has either been calibrated or a new one has been obtained. Ensure that the thermometer is being regularly calibrated to make sure that it is accurately measuring foods.
findings.citation_text: 4-203.11 Temperature Measuring Devices, Food. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES that are scaled only in Celsius or dually scaled in Celsius and Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±1°C in the intended range of use. (B) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2°F in the intended range of use.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The mop in the mop sink was observed to be placed directly in the basin of the mop sink. This does not allow for proper air drying of the mop after use. It is recommended to have a hook to allow it to air dry and drip into the mop sink. Due to the facility not having a hook or other piece of equipment that allows the mop to hang to air dry, it was recommended to place it in the wringer of the mop bucket. Ensure that mops are placed in a position that allows them to air-dry after use that does not soil walls, equipment, or supplies.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment:
4-302.14: The Quaternary ammonium test strips that are available in the facility are damaged and are not usable. Ensure that new test strips are obtained and are always usable and available to test the concentration of the sanitizer in the facility. A follow up is scheduled for 1/27/2025 to ensure that new Quaternary ammonium test strips have been obtained. 

Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. An employee was observed to wash his hands and not use a barrier to turn off the faucet after handwashing. Ensure that a barrier is always used after handwashing to avoid recontamination to the hands. CORRECTED- The staff was educated on proper handwashing. 

 (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
One of the two employees present does not have a signed reporting agreement on file. CORRECTED- Employee reviewed and signed a reporting agreement. Ensure employees are educated about foodborne illness symptoms and diagnoses that would restrict or exclude them from working. Keep signed reporting agreements on file for all employees.
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  [Pf]

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
Facility does not have a vomit/diarrhea clean up policy available. CORRECTED- Inspector printed a clean up policy and provided it to the facility. Keep a written vomit/diarrhea clean up policy available or provide a bodily fluid clean up kit.
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. [Pf]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Paper towels were not available in the womens restroom. CORRECTED- PIC refilled the paper towel dispenser. Ensure paper towels are always available at all handwashing sinks.
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
Ambient thermometers were not located in either the prep cooler or the 2 door storage cooler in the back. Provide ambient thermometers in all cold holding units.
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. [C]
